question: Assume today is 2026-09-05. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of new passenger cars (Pkw) registered in Germany in September 2026, as it will be first reported in the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt's (KBA) monthly press release on vehicle registrations.

target.what: Number of new passenger cars (Personenkraftwagen, Pkw) newly registered in Germany during September 2026, as first reported by the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt (KBA) in its monthly press release on vehicle registrations (Neuzulassungen von Personenkraftwagen). Counts first-time registrations of new Pkw (bra
target.cadence: monthly, typically published in the first days of the following month (early October 2026 for September 2026)
target.caveats: Target period is future relative to the 2026-09-05 cutoff, so no September 2026 data exist yet; estimate must be built from prior-year seasonality, year-to-date momentum, order books, and calendar effects. Working interpretation: KBA 'Neuzulassungen Pkw' total (all brands, incl. passenger-car-derive

candidates.hypothesis: September new-Pkw registrations follow a recurring seasonal pattern (September is typically a strong month due to the autumn order cycle and quarter-end), so prior Septembers and the 2026 year-to-date run-rate anchor the level. Target = recent monthly run-rate × September seasonal factor.
candidates.data_to_find: KBA monthly Neuzulassungen Pkw totals for September in each year 2015-2025 (and especially 2023, 2024, 2025), plus monthly totals Jan-Aug 2026 and full-year 2025, to compute the September seasonal index and the 2026 YTD level.

candidates.hypothesis: VDA and VDIK publish monthly Inlandsabsatz/Pkw-Neuzulassungen and order-intake figures that track KBA registrations closely; their September 2026 statements or August 2026 order backlog can constrain the September level. Target ≈ VDA domestic sales for September with a small coverage adjustment.
candidates.data_to_find: VDA monthly 'Inlandsabsatz Pkw' and 'Auftragseingang Inland' for 2025-2026, VDIK monthly registration commentary, and any September 2026 outlook/order-book statements published before cutoff.

candidates.hypothesis: Published 2026 full-year German Pkw registration forecasts (e.g., VDIK, ifo, analyst notes) can be decomposed into monthly paths; September 2026 = forecast annual total × September share of annual registrations.
candidates.data_to_find: Full-year 2026 German new-Pkw registration forecasts issued before 2026-09-05, and historical September share of annual registrations (2015-2025).

candidates.hypothesis: Any EV purchase incentive, company-car tax change, or CO2/fleet regulation effective in 2026 shifts September registrations (pull-forward or pull-back). Quantify the policy-driven increment relative to a baseline month.
candidates.data_to_find: German government EV/Kaufprämie or Dienstwagensteuer changes with effective dates in 2025-2026, and estimated monthly registration impact; also any scrappage or VAT effects.

candidates.hypothesis: Domestic registrations are supplied by domestic production plus imports minus exports; German OEM production and import volumes for September 2026 (or August run-rate) bound the registrations. Target ≈ (domestic production allocated to home market + imports) × registration share.
candidates.data_to_find: German passenger-car production (VDA/Statistisches Bundesamt) monthly 2026, import volumes of Pkw into Germany, and dealer inventory/stock levels.

candidates.hypothesis: Registrations depend on working days and KBA processing; September 2026 has 22 working days vs. prior Septembers, and quarter-end (Q3) pushes fleet/company registrations. Adjust the seasonal factor for working-day count.
candidates.data_to_find: Number of working days in September 2026 vs. September 2023-2025, and KBA monthly registration totals aligned to working-day counts to estimate per-working-day rate.

candidates.hypothesis: September total = sum over powertrain segments (BEV, PHEV, petrol, diesel, hybrid) of segment registrations; segment-level 2026 trends (BEV growth, diesel decline) can be projected from recent months and summed.
candidates.data_to_find: KBA monthly registrations by Kraftstoffart/segment for Jan-Aug 2026 and September 2025, plus BEV monthly growth trend.

candidates.hypothesis: German registrations co-move with EU/EFTA registrations (ACEA); ACEA September 2026 EU total × Germany's historical share of EU registrations gives a cross-check. Target = EU September registrations × German share.
candidates.data_to_find: ACEA monthly new passenger car registrations for EU/EFTA Jan-Aug 2026 and September 2025, and Germany's share of EU registrations historically.

methods.rationale: September 2025 level (p42) scaled by the YoY growth of the latest observed month (August 2026 p86/p223 vs August 2025). Failure mode: August YoY may not carry into September.

methods.rationale: August 2026 level (p223) times a September seasonal uplift factor (a2) derived from historical September-vs-August MoM changes (p45, p59). Captures the autumn order-cycle effect; failure mode is that the seasonal factor varies year to year.

methods.rationale: September 2025 level (p42) times a YoY growth factor (a1) anchored on August 2026 +2.6% (p224), July +1.2% (p247) and YTD +5.1% (p248). Directly uses the target month's prior-year value; failure mode is that September 2025 was unusually strong, so the YoY factor may be lower.

assumptions.name: September 2026 YoY growth factor vs September 2025
assumptions.rationale: August 2026 was +2.6% YoY (p224), July +1.2% (p247), YTD Jan-Jul +5.1% (p248); order intake +4% (p96) and BEV orders +62% (p97) support modest growth. September 2025 was a strong month (+12.8%, p44), so a repeat is unlikely; central 1.03 with wide range reflecting month-to-month volatility.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 registrations track the recent YoY momentum and no major policy pull-forward occurs.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a large September 2026 policy-driven surge or collapse (e.g., subsidy deadline) or a September order-intake collapse.

assumptions.name: September seasonal factor relative to August run-rate
assumptions.rationale: September 2025 was +13.7% MoM vs August 2025 (p45); September 2024 was +5.8% MoM (p59). September 2026 has 22 working days and no holidays (p339, p342), similar to prior Septembers; central 1.10 with wide range.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 follows the historical September-vs-August seasonal uplift.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 lacks the usual autumn order-cycle uplift or has an unusual working-day pattern.

previous_assumptions.applies_when: The September-over-August seasonal uplift in 2026 is similar to 2025.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 registrations fell below August 2026 or rose far above the historical September uplift.

methods.label: m1
methods.rationale: September 2025 total (p598) scaled by the Jan-Aug 2026 YoY growth signal (p628/p630, +5%). The signal is a cumulative YoY growth for the same year, available for 2026; the route transfers last September's level forward using the year-to-date momentum. Shared dependency: both target and signal are KBA totals; the route assumes YTD growth carries into September.
notes: mixed % and non-% units; dropped the minority

methods.label: m2

p223.role: August 2026 Pkw new registrations in Germany (KBA)

a2.role: September seasonal factor relative to August run-rate

methods.rationale: Applies the recurring September-over-August seasonal uplift (anchored on the +13.7% MoM seen in September 2025, p602) to the latest observed monthly level (August 2026, p223). Failure mode: the 2026 EV subsidy may have pulled demand forward, weakening the usual September uplift.

methods.label: m3

p42.role: September 2025 Pkw new registrations in Germany (KBA)

a1.role: September 2026 YoY growth factor vs September 2025

methods.rationale: Anchors on the same calendar month last year (p42) and applies a YoY growth factor grounded in the 2026 YTD +5% and August +2.6-3% momentum, with BEV strength offsetting ICE decline. Failure mode: a policy-driven September distortion (subsidy pull-forward) not reflected in the recent run-rate.

weight_basis.m2: B1 of 2 blocks; geometric mean of blocks
weight_basis.m3: B2 of 2 blocks; geometric mean of blocks

combination.weight_gate: off: inverse backtest-error weights need a bank-level gate (>= 30 scored questions with >= 2 backtested routes, hit rate >= 0.7; METHODS_ZH 4.1), which has not been run

m3.note: Monte Carlo width below the default, not used to narrow

interval.rule: several blocks: root mean square of the block widths, times the Birge ratio when it exceeds 1

baseline.rule: seasonal naive: the target's value for the same calendar period last year

kept.name: September 2026 YoY growth factor vs September 2025
kept.rationale: Jan-Aug 2026 cumulative is +5% YoY (p630) and August +2.6-3% (p584/p629); BEV strength (p587, p636) offsets petrol/diesel decline (p596, p597). September 2025 was already a strong month (+12.8%, p600), so a modest further YoY gain is plausible; range spans a flat-to-weak market to continued BEV-led
kept.applies_when: September 2026 market growth resembles the recent run-rate rather than a policy-driven pull-forward or pull-back.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence of a September 2026 subsidy cliff or order collapse that pushes YoY growth outside the range.

A factor near 1.1 with a wide range captures the recurring September uplift, tempered by the risk that the 2026
kept.applies_when: The September-over-August seasonal uplift in 2026 is similar to 2025.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 registrations fell below August 2026 or rose far above the historical September uplift.

The best estimate for new passenger car (Pkw) registrations in Germany during September 2026, as first reported by the KBA, is 237,187 vehicle (80% model-based interval 165,902 to 339,103 vehicle).

Evidence: one route applies the recurring September-over-August seasonal uplift (1.1, range 0.7706 to 1.541) to the observed August 2026 level of 212,563 new passenger car registrations; the other scales the observed September 2025 level of 235,528 new passenger car registrations by an assumed YoY factor (1.03, range 0.92 to 1.15). The two blocks were combined with equal weight because their inputs overlap; the interval is conditional on these assumptions, not a demonstrated accuracy guarantee.

Main risk: a policy-driven pull-forward of demand (2026 EV subsidy) weakening the usual September uplift. Missing evidence that would most improve the estimate: September 2026 order books or early-month registration data.

Unit of the estimate: vehicle (new passenger car registrations; total for 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-30).

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a1 September 2026 YoY growth factor vs September 2025: 1.03 [n], range 0.92 to 1.15 (range widened by code); used by m3. Overturned by: Evidence of a September 2026 subsidy cliff or order collapse that pushes YoY growth outside the range.
- a2 September seasonal factor relative to August run-rate: 1.1 [n], range 0.7706 to 1.541 (range widened by code); used by m2. Overturned by: Evidence that September 2026 registrations fell below August 2026 or rose far above the historical September uplift.

Method details (computed by code):
- m2 formula_mc: p223 * a2; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 156,941 to 343,061; result unit (vehicle/month) * 1 month converted to vehicle; own 80% width x/÷1.48 (Monte Carlo of the formula inputs)
- m3 formula_mc: p42 * a1; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 196,065 to 300,226; result unit (vehicle/month) * 1 month converted to vehicle; own 80% width x/÷1.38 (no error evidence, code's default width)
- Combination: 2 block(s), equal weight per block (methods whose inputs overlap by at least half form one block; backtest errors set widths, not weights): B1 = m2: 231,887 (width x/÷1.48, Monte Carlo of the formula inputs); B2 = m3: 242,609 (width x/÷1.38, no error evidence, code's default width). Estimate = the geometric mean of the two blocks.
- Interval: root mean square of the block widths x/÷1.43; Birge ratio 0.11 (not above one, so no widening); final width x/÷1.43.
- Seasonal naive baseline (not combined): 235,528 (2025, from m1); the estimate is +0.7% against it.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.

The magnitude gate (v2.15d) asks the model once, without retrieval, for a rough estimate; whether the evidence-based estimate is more than 2x above or below it can carry the model's memory of the target into one repair. The rough number itself never enters a computation or a prompt; the estimate before that repair is kept in judge_rounds[-1].magnitude_checks[0]. The gate is off in the own-history ablation.
